examples.ko: 아침에 밭에 서릿발이 허옇게 서 있었어요.
examples.en: In the morning, white frost spikes were standing in the field.

examples.ko: 서릿발을 밟으니 발밑에서 서걱서걱 소리가 났어요.
examples.en: When I stepped on the frost spikes, they crunched under my feet.
Because of frost spikes, the ground heaves in winter.
Everyone froze at the icy-cold look in his eyes.

examples.ko: 선생님의 서릿발 같은 호통에 교실이 조용해졌어요.
examples.en: The classroom went quiet at the teacher's stern scolding.

examples.ko: 서릿발에 뿌리가 들려서 보리 싹이 시들었어요.
examples.en: The barley sprouts withered because frost spikes lifted their roots.

explain: '서리'는 얼어붙은 흰 결정을 넓게 말하고, '서릿발'은 땅에서 기둥처럼 솟은 모양에 초점을 둬요. 비유로 차갑고 엄한 기세를 말할 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 서릿발 같은 목소리로 꾸짖어서 아무도 대답하지 못했어요.
phrases.en: He scolded in such a stern voice that nobody could answer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기세나 말투가 차갑고 엄해서 두렵게 느껴진다는 뜻이에요. 주로 호통, 눈빛, 명령에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the force or tone is cold and severe enough to feel frightening. It is mainly used for scolding, looks and orders.
phrases.en_equiv: stern as ice; icy and severe

explain_en: '서리' is the frozen white crystals in general, while '서릿발' focuses on the columns standing up from the ground. It is also used figuratively for a cold, stern force.

en: to be chilly; to be suddenly cold

examples.en: A cold wind is blowing, and the back of my neck feels chilly.
The season has come when the air is chilly morning and evening.
When I stepped on the floor barefoot, my feet felt a cold shock.

examples.ko: 그 말을 듣는 순간 가슴이 선뜩했어요.
examples.en: The moment I heard those words, my heart gave a chill.
I felt chilly after my shower, so I put on a jacket.

examples.ko: 가을이 되니 이불 밖이 선뜩하게 느껴져요.
examples.en: Now that it's autumn, it feels chilly outside the blanket.

explain: '서늘하다'와 비슷하지만 선뜩하다는 갑자기 차가운 것에 닿거나 차갑게 느껴지는 순간의 느낌이 강해요. 놀라서 가슴이 서늘해지는 느낌에도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: A chilly wind started to blow in the evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ'을 붙여 바람 같은 명사를 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: -ㄴ lets it modify nouns like wind.

phrases.en: My back suddenly felt chilly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어지다'로 느낌이 갑자기 변했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: -아/어지다 shows the feeling suddenly changed.

phrases.en: The water is colder than I thought, so my feet feel a chill.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체 활용형이라서 말할 때 바로 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The haeyo form, ready to use in conversation.

explain_en: It is similar to '서늘하다' (cool), but 선뜩하다 stresses the sudden moment of touching or feeling something cold. It can also describe the chill you feel in your chest when startled.

t90.ax: I felt chilly after my shower, so I put on a jacket.

examples.en: A flash of light streaked across the dark sky.
The camera flash dazzled my eyes.
A good idea suddenly flashed into my mind.
I squeezed my eyes shut at the strong flash.
The dark night sky suddenly lit up with a flash.

examples.ko: 멀리서 섬광을 보고 나서 천둥소리를 들었어요.
examples.en: I saw a flash in the distance and then heard thunder.

explain: 번개나 불빛처럼 아주 짧고 강하게 번쩍이는 빛을 말해요. 일상에서는 '번쩍임', '번개'라고 더 자주 말하고, '섬광'은 글이나 뉴스, 묘사하는 말에서 많이 보여요. '섬광처럼 스치다'는 생각이 갑자기 떠오를 때 비유로 써요.

phrases.en: A flash of light lit up the night sky.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빛이 아주 짧고 강하게 나타날 때 쓰는 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural pairing for a very short, strong burst of light.

phrases.en: A good idea flashed through my mind like lightning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각이 갑자기 떠오르는 순간을 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use for a thought that suddenly comes to mind.
phrases.en_equiv: to flash by like a spark

phrases.en: I saw a bright flash outside the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: 섬광보다 쉽고 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, more everyday word than 섬광.

explain_en: It means a very short, strong flash of light like lightning. In everyday talk people more often say '번쩍임' or '번개', while '섬광' appears in writing, news and descriptions. '섬광처럼 스치다' is used figuratively when an idea suddenly comes to mind.

examples.en: The cat takes a nap in a sunny spot.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 양지바른 곳에 앉아 있고 싶어요.
examples.en: In winter, I want to sit in a sunny place.
I hung the laundry out in a sunny spot.
This house gets sun, so it is warm even in winter.
My grandmother dries beans in a sunny spot.
Plants grow better in the sun than in the shade.

explain: '양지'의 반대말은 '음지'로, 햇볕이 드는 곳과 그늘진 곳을 구분할 때 써요. '양지바르다'는 햇빛이 잘 드는 곳을 묘사하는 말이에요. '양지'는 따뜻하고 좋은 곳이라는 느낌이 있어서, 편한 처지를 비유할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: I sat on a bench on the sunny side.
phrases.nuance_ko: 햇볕이 드는 쪽이라는 뜻으로, '양지'보다 방향을 말하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the side that gets sun, a bit more directional than '양지'.

phrases.en: In winter, sitting in a sunny spot is warm.
phrases.nuance_ko: '양지'를 장소로 쓰는 가장 쉬운 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The simplest way to use '양지' as a place.

phrases.en: The sunny spot is warm, but the shady spot is cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말과 함께 비교해서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to compare with its opposite, '음지' (shade).

explain_en: The opposite of '양지' is '음지' (shade): sunny spots versus shaded ones. '양지바르다' describes a place that gets plenty of sun. Because '양지' feels warm and good, it can also stand figuratively for a comfortable position.

en: to be obvious; to be evident

examples.en: Outside the window, the spring air is already unmistakable.

examples.ko: 그 사람 얼굴에 피곤한 기색이 완연해요.
examples.en: Signs of tiredness are clearly visible on his face.

examples.ko: 산에 가 보니 가을 분위기가 완연한 것 같아요.
examples.en: Going to the mountain, it seems autumn is fully here.

examples.ko: 그의 표정에 긴장한 모습이 완연해서 걱정됐어요.
examples.en: His nervousness showed clearly on his face, so I was worried.
Once spring has fully arrived, let's go on a picnic together.
Joy is plainly written on the child's face.

explain: 계절의 느낌이나 표정, 기색이 눈에 분명히 보일 때 써요. '봄기운이 완연하다', '피곤한 기색이 완연하다'처럼 짝이 되는 말이 있고, 일상 대화보다는 글이나 방송에서 더 자주 들려요. 더 쉬운 말은 '뚜렷하다'예요.

phrases.en: It's now fully autumn, so the weather is cool.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 말을 꾸미는 형태로, 계절이 눈에 분명히 느껴질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, used when a season is clearly noticeable.

phrases.en: His fatigue showed clearly on his face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사형으로 쓰면 표정이나 기색이 눈에 분명히 보인다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form means an expression or sign is clearly visible.

phrases.en: The difference between the two photos is clear.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 쉬운 말로, 일상 대화에서 '완연하다' 대신 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word that can replace 완연하다 in everyday talk.

explain_en: Literary — a season or sign is fully apparent (봄기운이 완연하다) It is used when a season's feel, an expression or a sign is plainly visible. It has typical partners like '봄기운이 완연하다' and '피곤한 기색이 완연하다', and you hear it more in writing and broadcasts than in casual talk. A simpler word is '뚜렷하다'.

t90.ax: Joy is plainly written on the child's face.

examples.ko: 복도 형광등이 오래돼서 밤이 되면 어둡고 으스스해요.
examples.en: The hallway lights are old, so it's dark and eerie at night.
When the cold wind blew, my body shivered.
I feel chilly, as if I'm catching a cold.

examples.ko: 으스스한 이야기를 들으니 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: After hearing a creepy story, I can't sleep.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 폐가 앞을 지나니 으스스했어요.
examples.en: Passing the abandoned house on a rainy day felt eerie.
I feel a chill in the mornings and evenings.

explain: 몸이 차갑거나 무서워서 소름 끼칠 때 쓰는 말이에요. 보통 '으스스 춥다/떨리다'로 쓰고, '으스스하다'로 분위기가 무서울 때도 써요. 감기 기운이 있을 때 쓰는 말로도 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I felt a chill when I woke up in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감기 기운이 있을 때처럼 몸이 차가운 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A chilly feeling in the body, like the start of a cold.

phrases.en: That house has an eerie atmosphere.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소가 무서운 느낌일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a place feels creepy.

phrases.example: 무서운 이야기를 들으니 으스스 소름이 돋았어요.
phrases.en: I got goosebumps hearing the scary story.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무서워서 몸에 소름이 생길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when fear gives you goosebumps.

explain_en: It describes the feeling when you are cold or scared and get goosebumps. It is usually '으스스 춥다/떨리다', and '으스스하다' is used for a creepy atmosphere. It is also natural for the chills you get when coming down with a cold.

examples.en: Tomorrow is Ipdong, so the weather is chilly.
Now that Ipdong has passed, the morning air is cold.
Many households start making kimchi for winter around Ipdong.
This year Ipdong is around November 7.
Around Ipdong, the first ice sometimes forms.
Some homes turn on the heating from Ipdong.

explain: 24절기 중 하나로, 달력에서 겨울이 시작되는 날로 표시돼요. 보통 11월 초이고, 입춘, 입하, 입추처럼 '입-'으로 시작하는 절기 이름과 함께 알아 두면 좋아요. 날씨 뉴스나 달력에서 볼 수 있어요.

phrases.en: Around Ipdong, people start making kimchi for the winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입동 즈음의 시기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to refer to the period around Ipdong.

phrases.en: Once Ipdong came, it really got cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 절기가 시작되었음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that this solar term has arrived.

phrases.en: My family makes kimchi on Ipdong.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입동과 관련된 한국의 풍습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about Korean customs tied to Ipdong.

explain_en: First day of winter on the solar calendar, around November 7. It is one of the 24 solar terms and is marked on the calendar as the start of winter, usually in early November. It's good to learn it together with 입춘, 입하 and 입추, the other terms that begin with '입-'. You can see it in weather news and on calendars.

en: to hesitate; to stall; to flinch

examples.ko: 길 앞에서 개를 보고 잠깐 주춤했어요.
examples.en: I saw a dog in front of me and paused for a moment.

examples.ko: 갑자기 소리가 나서 아이가 주춤하며 뒤를 봤어요.
examples.en: A sudden sound made the child flinch and look back.
The popularity slowed for a while and then rose again.
It was a month when sales slowed because of the rain.

examples.ko: 그는 문 앞에서 주춤해서 들어가지 못했어요.
examples.en: He hesitated at the door and couldn't go in.

examples.ko: 주춤하지 말고 하고 싶은 말을 해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't hold back; say what you want to say.

explain: 사람이 놀라거나 망설여서 몸이 잠깐 멈출 때 쓰고, 오르던 숫자나 인기가 잠시 멈출 때도 써요. 완전히 멈추는 게 아니라 잠깐이에요. '망설이다'는 마음이 정해지지 않는 것이고, '주춤하다'는 몸이나 흐름이 잠깐 멈추는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: At the loud noise, the child backed away hesitantly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주춤주춤'은 여러 번 머뭇거리는 모습이에요. 뒤로 물러설 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '주춤주춤' shows repeated hesitation, often when stepping back.

phrases.en: That singer's popularity has stalled lately.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오르던 인기나 숫자가 잠깐 멈출 때 써요. 완전히 끝난 것은 아니에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when rising popularity or numbers pause briefly, not fully stop.

phrases.en: He walked forward without hesitating.
phrases.nuance_ko: 망설이지 않고 바로 움직였다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means he moved straight on without pausing.

explain_en: Body stops briefly in surprise or fear (갑자기 비가 오자 사람들이 잠시 주춤했어요.) It is used when a person stops for a moment out of surprise or hesitation, and when rising numbers or popularity pause briefly. It is not a full stop, just a short one. 망설이다 is about being undecided in your mind, while 주춤하다 is a body or trend pausing for a moment.

t90.ax: Don't hold back; say what you want to say.

examples.en: I dipped my feet into the ice-cold winter sea.

examples.ko: 겨울 아침 바닥이 차디차서 양말을 두 켤레 신었어요.
examples.en: The floor was freezing on the winter morning, so I wore two pairs of socks.

examples.ko: 손이 차디차네요. 이 장갑을 껴 보세요.
examples.en: Your hands are ice cold. Try putting on these gloves.
That person answered coldly and turned away.
The water is freezing, so get in carefully.

examples.ko: 방이 차디차지 않게 보일러를 켜 두었어요.
examples.en: I left the heating on so the room wouldn't be freezing.

explain: '차다'를 강하게 말한 표현이에요. 말할 때는 '엄청 차다'를 더 자주 쓰고, '차디찬' 모양은 글이나 노래 가사에서 자주 보여요. 사람의 냉정한 태도를 비유할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: A freezing wind is blowing and my ears hurt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 매우 차가운 바람을 강하게 표현하는 말이에요. 글이나 노래에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A strong way to describe a very cold wind, often seen in writing and songs.

phrases.en: The floor is really cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때는 '차디차다'보다 이 표현을 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In speech, this is used more often than '차디차다'.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 저를 차디찬 눈빛으로 봤어요.
phrases.en: That person looked at me with an icy stare.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 냉정한 태도를 비유할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used figuratively for a person's cold attitude.

explain_en: Emphatic: extremely cold, like icy water. It is a stronger version of '차다' (cold). In speech people more often say '엄청 차다', while the form '차디찬' appears often in writing and song lyrics. It can also describe a cold, unfeeling attitude.

examples.en: At the zoo, a chimpanzee was eating a banana.
I went to the zoo to see the smart chimpanzees.
I saw a chimpanzee family in a documentary.
The child made everyone laugh by imitating a chimpanzee.
Humans and chimpanzees have a lot in common.
That scholar taught sign language to a chimpanzee.

explain: '원숭이'는 꼬리가 있는 종류를 주로 말하고, 침팬지는 꼬리가 없는 '유인원'이에요. 고릴라, 오랑우탄도 같은 유인원이라서 침팬지와 함께 소개돼요. 사람과 가장 가까운 동물로 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 침팬지 무리가 나무 위에서 쉬고 있어요.
phrases.en: A group of chimpanzees is resting in a tree.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 마리가 함께 있을 때 '무리'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 무리 when many are together.

phrases.en: A baby chimpanzee was born at the zoo.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새끼 침팬지를 말할 때 앞에 '아기'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 아기 in front to mean a young chimpanzee.

phrases.en: A chimpanzee is an ape.
phrases.nuance_ko: 침팬지가 속한 큰 분류의 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name of the larger group that chimpanzees belong to.

explain_en: 원숭이 mostly refers to tailed monkeys, while 침팬지 is a tailless ape, a 유인원. Gorillas and orangutans are apes too, so they are introduced together with chimpanzees. Chimpanzees often appear as the animal closest to humans.

examples.en: Suddenly raindrops began to patter down.

examples.ko: 비가 그친 뒤 나뭇잎에서 물방울이 후두둑 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: After the rain stopped, drops pattered down from the leaves.
Hail pelted down on the roof.
When I shook the chestnut tree, chestnuts rained down.

examples.ko: 창문에 후두둑 소리가 나서 밖을 봤어요.
examples.en: I heard a pattering on the window and looked outside.
When I opened the bag, coins spilled out all at once.

explain: 굵은 빗방울, 열매, 작은 물건이 연달아 떨어지는 소리나 모습에 써요. '후두둑 후두둑'처럼 반복해서도 말해요. 후드득과 비슷해서 서로 바꿔 써도 자연스러운 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: Raindrops pattered against the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: '후두둑'과 비슷해서 바꿔 써도 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 후두둑 and interchangeable with it.

phrases.example: 지붕 위로 우박이 후두둑 후두둑 떨어졌어요.
phrases.en: Hail kept pattering down on the roof.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반복해서 말하면 소리가 계속 이어지는 느낌이 더 커져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Repeating it makes the continuous sound stronger.

phrases.en: When the wind blew, persimmons fell with a patter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비뿐 아니라 열매나 작은 물건이 떨어질 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Works not only for rain but also for fruit or small things falling.

explain_en: It is used for the sound or sight of thick raindrops, fruit or small things falling one after another. You can also repeat it, as in '후두둑 후두둑'. It is close to 후드득, and in many cases you can swap the two naturally.

examples.ko: 이 규칙은 강제성이 없어서 지키는 사람이 적어요.
examples.en: This rule isn't binding, so few people follow it.

examples.ko: 법에 강제성이 있어야 모두가 따를 거예요.
examples.en: Everyone will follow it only if the law is enforceable.
There is no compulsion at all in club activities.
Because it was a compulsory system, the backlash was big.

examples.ko: 이 지침은 권고일 뿐 강제성을 가지지는 않아요.
examples.en: This guideline is only a recommendation and has no binding force.

examples.ko: 강제성 때문에 참여하는 거라면 오래 못 가요.
examples.en: If you take part only because you are forced to, it won't last long.

explain: 주로 '강제성이 있다/없다', '강제성을 띠다'로 써요. 규칙, 제도, 참여처럼 억지로 따르게 하는 정도를 말할 때 많이 나와요. 사람의 태도를 말할 때는 '강압적'이 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 이 캠페인은 강제성이 없어서 참여는 자유예요.
phrases.en: This campaign isn't compulsory, so participation is voluntary.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반드시 따라야 하는 것이 아닐 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something doesn't have to be followed.

phrases.example: 그 지침은 점점 강제성을 띠고 있어요.
phrases.en: That guideline is gradually becoming binding.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래는 아니었지만 억지로 따라야 하는 성격이 생길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something takes on a compulsory nature.

phrases.example: 이 제도는 강제성이 약해서 효과가 적어요.
phrases.en: This system has weak enforcement, so its effect is small.
phrases.nuance_ko: 규칙을 따르게 하는 힘이 크지 않다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the force making people follow the rule is small.

explain_en: It is mostly used as '강제성이 있다/없다' (is/is not binding) or '강제성을 띠다' (carry compulsion). It often appears when talking about how strongly rules, systems or participation are imposed. For a person's attitude, '강압적' is more natural.

t90.ax: This rule isn't binding, so few people follow it.

examples.en: The typhoon suddenly changed direction and went west.
The car in front turned sharply, so I was startled.
The company made a sharp turn toward going overseas.
If public opinion suddenly swings, policy changes too.
Hold the handle when the boat turns sharply.
Citizens were flustered by the government's sharply changed policy.

explain: 움직이는 것이 방향을 확 바꿀 때와 계획이나 방침이 갑자기 달라질 때 모두 써요. 방침이나 여론을 말할 때는 '급선회하다'가 '바뀌다'보다 훨씬 갑작스러운 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: The company's policy did a U-turn overnight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거 해요체로, 이미 방향이 확 바뀐 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past polite form for a direction that has already changed sharply.

phrases.en: I saw a car turning sharply and quickly got out of the way.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 주는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form placed before a noun.

phrases.example: 학교의 시험 방침이 급선회해서 학생들이 혼란스러워해요.
phrases.en: The school's exam policy suddenly reversed, so students are confused.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계획이나 규칙이 갑자기 달라질 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for a sudden change of plans or rules.

explain_en: It is used both when a moving thing suddenly changes direction and when a plan or policy suddenly shifts. For policies or opinion, it feels much more abrupt than '바뀌다'.

examples.ko: 이번 협상은 막후에서 많은 일이 있었어요.
examples.en: A lot went on behind the scenes in this negotiation.

examples.ko: 막후 실세가 따로 있다는 소문이 돌았어요.
examples.en: A rumor went around that the real power-holder is someone behind the scenes.

examples.ko: 영화 촬영의 막후 이야기를 책으로 냈어요.
examples.en: She published a book of behind-the-scenes stories from filming.

examples.ko: 막후 교섭 끝에 두 나라가 합의했어요.
examples.en: After behind-the-scenes talks, the two countries reached an agreement.

examples.ko: 그는 이제 막후로 물러나 조용히 지내요.
examples.en: He has now stepped back behind the scenes and lives quietly.
Let's give applause to the unsung heroes behind the scenes.

explain: 뉴스에서 '막후 협상', '막후 실세'처럼 공개되지 않은 곳에서 일이 움직일 때 써요. 영화나 방송 이야기에서는 '비하인드'와 비슷하게 쓰여요. '막후 실세'는 대체로 비판하는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.example: 두 나라는 막후 협상을 이어 가고 있어요.
phrases.en: The two countries are continuing behind-the-scenes talks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 공개되지 않은 협상을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in the news for talks held out of public view.

phrases.example: 누군가 막후에서 움직이고 있는 것 같아요.
phrases.en: It seems someone is pulling strings behind the scenes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 드러나지 않게 일을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone works things out of sight.
phrases.en_equiv: to pull strings behind the scenes

phrases.en: I'll tell you the behind-the-scenes story of the movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방송이나 영화 이야기에서 '비하인드'처럼 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used like 'behind the scenes' in talk about shows and films.

explain_en: In news it appears in '막후 협상' and '막후 실세' when things are decided out of public view. In talk about films and TV it is close to 'behind the scenes'. '막후 실세' usually carries a critical tone.
